title: Characteristic-two hyperelliptic curves of every genus from an Artin–Schreier equation

author_roles.attribution_basis: Official solution PDF header; course attribution, not a claim of individually identified handwriting.

source_title: ETH Algebraic Geometry II, Autumn 2017 — official Solutions 14
difficulty_reason: For every g>=1 in characteristic2, the author constructs a second affine chart at infinity, checks nonsingularity using the characteristic-two Jacobian, glues a finite separable degree-two map to P1, and identifies its direct-image sheaf as O plus O(-(g+1) infinity) to compute the genus. The infinity chart and transition/direct-image construction are carried by this problem rather than supplied as prerequisites; ordinary Jacobian and P1 line-bundle cohomology are standard prerequisites.
statement_scope: Official Sheet14 Q2: for any algebraically closed field k of characteristic2 and any integer g>=1, the smooth projective curve with affine equation y^2+y=x^(2g+1) is hyperelliptic of genus g. This uses the course explicit degree-two-cover convention including g=1.

statement_spans.label: Printed Q2 beginning Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic2 and let g>=1, through the sentence asserting hyperelliptic curves of every genus>=1; below Q1 caution and before Solution.

proof_spans.label: Q2 Solution beginning Set a(x,y):=y^2+y-x^(2g+1), through the final h^1=0+g=g display, ending before printed Q3. Includes infinity chart and transition, finite separable double cover, direct-image split and genus computation.
